question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=\frac{1}{2}(x+4)(x+k)$ is $x=-\frac{3}{2}.$ The value of $k=$
question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{3}{2},$ we will set our result equal to $-\frac{3}{2}.$ 

From the equation $y=\frac{1}{2}(x+4)(x+k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=-k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4-k}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-k-4}{2} & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ -k-4 & =-3 \\ -k & =1 \\ k & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
